title: Muslim League backed Satheesan in Keralam CM race, now gets payback from Congress faction
content: Kozhikode: For the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), being sidelined by its principal ally, the Indian National Congress (INC), at the national level is hardly a new experience. However, the party's perceived exclusion from key INDIA bloc engagements in Delhi — including the protest rally at Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the opposition delegation's meeting with the President of India — has given a new dimension to its sense of marginalisation. What makes these incidents particularly significant is the IUML's belief that the reasons for its alleged neglect may have changed. During Rahul Gandhi's first electoral outing in Wayanad in 2019, the controversy over allegations that the Congress had sought to keep the IUML's green flags out of campaign rallies, fearing political backlash in North India because of their perceived resemblance to the Pakistani flag, was seen as a reflection of the Congress's unease over being visibly associated with a Muslim political outfit on the national stage. The IUML now suspects, however, that the problem runs deeper into the Congress's own political and organisational equations. The party increasingly suspects that internal factionalism within the Congress, particularly the resentment of a section of its Keralam leadership over the IUML's growing influence in the new Congress-led government and its support for V D Satheesan as Chief Minister, is behind its exclusion from national-level events. Despite being a significant constituent of the opposition alliance, the IUML felt conspicuously pushed to the margins during the Ramlila Maidan rally and the symbolic public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Its senior leader was allegedly denied an opportunity to address the gathering. The party's sense of exclusion was further compounded when its representative was initially left out of the delegation that met the President of India, even as representatives of other INDIA bloc constituents participated. For the IUML, these were not merely protocol oversights or isolated organisational lapses, but signs of deliberate political distancing. The party suspects that a section of the Congress with considerable influence in Keralam is actively working to limit its political visibility and influence within the INDIA bloc. The IUML had openly supported Satheesan for the Chief Minister's post during the tussle over the top position following the Keralam Assembly election, taking a clear stand to prevent political uncertainty in the state. The party now suspects that this position may have provoked resentment among a section of the Congress leadership. The IUML leadership has decided to take up the issue with the Congress high command. Party leaders are planning to meet senior Congress leaders, including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Priyanka Gandhi, in the coming days. The party's state president, Panakkad Sadiq Ali Shihab Thangal, who is currently abroad, is expected to return to Malappuram on Tuesday, after which further discussions will be held. Muslim League MPs and party workers have been an active presence in the series of protests organised by the INDIA bloc in Delhi. It was Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge who invited IUML state president Panakkad Sadiq Ali Shihab Thangal to the mega rally at Ramlila Maidan. As Thangal was abroad, the IUML leadership deputed its national general secretary and Keralam Industries and IT Minister P K Kunhalikutty to represent the party in Delhi. The IUML had expected Kunhalikutty to be invited to address the rally, but that did not happen. The party is particularly unhappy with the decision to give CPM general secretary M A Baby an opportunity to speak while denying the same to the League's representative. Initially, the IUML was not included in the delegation scheduled to visit Rashtrapati Bhavan to submit a memorandum against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar...
